title: Chapter 171: Something Wrong with Qin Guang
html:
The wardrobe contained nothing else. Chen Ge closed it and took several photographs.

“Four blood-red nails pierce its corners, and clear tape seals every gap. Those protections may be why it survived so long inside the Third Sick Hall.”

He tried pulling out one nail but could not move it. All four were driven so deeply that they seemed fused with the wood.

“These nails are unusual. I should return after sunrise and remove them properly.”

He had spent too long in the director’s office and knew nothing of what now waited outside.

When he left the rest area, the white cat leaped onto his shoulder and refused to climb down. Chen Ge crept toward the office entrance, wary of stepping directly into an ambush by the nurse or the twisted-faced man.

Hammer raised, he listened through the door. After ten seconds, a peculiar sound reached him: doors opening and closing down the corridor, one after another, as though someone were searching every room.

He eased the office door open. Far down the seemingly endless corridor, something swayed through the darkness, its silhouette forming and dissolving as it moved between rooms.

“A white nurse’s uniform. Is she searching for the notebook?” Chen Ge tightened his grip on the hammer and weighed confrontation against retreat. Her mangled body forced her into a staggering gait, yet she moved surprisingly fast. From a distance, her approach was terrifying.

“She nearly discovered me on the third floor. Only that other door opening prevented a fight. Leaving her active creates another threat, so I should bait her with the notebook and attack while I still have surprise.”

Remaining as calm as possible, he chose the strategy offering him the greatest advantage.

“The director’s office is spacious. Even if the first blow fails, I’ll have room to continue. This is also a chance to test the cleaver against a spirit.”

He placed the notebook before the wardrobe, secured the letters, and climbed inside with the cat. After adjusting into a workable position, he waited. Several minutes later, the office door opened.

The nurse spotted the notebook at once but did not rush toward it. She appeared wary of the wardrobe and hesitated before staggering inside.

Chen Ge tracked every movement. When she bent for the notebook, he exploded from hiding and swung the hammer into her. The blow further distorted her already broken form.

Before she could recover, he drew the cleaver. Its red wrapping fell away as the blade sliced through the uniform with a sharp hiss. No blood spilled, but part of the nurse’s body vanished.

“This cleaver is useable!”

Pain and fury twisted the corpse’s face. Shrieking, she opened her jaws and lunged for his head.

Chen Ge raised the cleaver but had underestimated her ferocity. Unlike a living opponent, she did not slow when the blade cut her; if anything, she accelerated.

The weapon wounded her, but not quickly enough. Her ruined face closed to within inches of his own.

Death was a heartbeat away when the white cat sprang from his shoulder onto the nurse’s face. The vicious stray disrupted her attack, forcing her jaws toward Chen Ge’s arm instead.

He twisted left and right beneath the barrage. Something clicked against his wrist and fell, but he ignored it, concentrating entirely on cutting apart the spirit.

No blood appeared, yet each slash reduced her size and made her form waver. After countless blows, she vanished completely, leaving only the shredded uniform on the floor.

“It’s over?”

Before he could celebrate, commotion erupted in the corridor. Several things were approaching at once.

“I can’t stay. If they surround me, I’m dead.” He snatched up his backpack and retreated with hammer in one hand and cleaver in the other. At the stairwell, just as he paused for breath, his phone vibrated.

A mission-completion alert?The screen left him feeling cheated. It was Liu Dao. I need to tell them never to call during a livestream. One badly timed ring could kill me.

Chen Ge answered the call with a whisper. “I’m hanging up if there’s nothing important.”

“Quick look at your livestream room!” Liu Dao sounded quite excited.

“What?” He opened the livestream page and stared. His audience had surged to three hundred thousand and continued climbing fast enough to pass four hundred thousand within minutes.

“What happened? Is the platform malfunctioning?” He immediately changed the livestream title to advertise his Haunted House and added its address to the description.

“The platform is fine, but something is definitely wrong with Qin Guang. After he entered a classroom at Mu Yang High School, his feed went black. No one knows why. I assumed it was an effect, but the blackout has lasted twenty-five minutes. Five minutes without video is disastrous for a professional stream. His team must have suffered an accident.”

Liu Dao grew more excited with every word. “It’s a gift from heaven. The platform promoted supernatural livestreaming because of him, but his viewers got only a black screen. They searched for similar broadcasts. Since yours is the only alternative—and its content and quality are much better—they came over and stayed.”

Following that trajectory, half a million viewers was entirely possible—a dream audience for a new host like Chen Ge.
